steps.body: In a right triangle, name the two sides that form the right angle (the **legs**) a and b, and the side opposite the right angle (the **hypotenuse**) c. The **Pythagorean theorem** says a² + b² = c². Compare two equal outer squares, each with side length a + b, as the same four right triangles are rearranged.
Check one example, then return to the general proof.

widget.prompt: For a right triangle with legs 3 and 4, what is c²? This checks one example; the rearrangement diagram gives the general proof.

authoredStages.title: Example leg squares
authoredStages.body: In this example, the square on the leg of length 3 has area 9, and the square on the leg of length 4 has area 16.

authoredStages.title: Example area sum
authoredStages.body: For this triangle, the two leg-square areas add to 9 + 16 = 25 square units.

authoredStages.title: Verify this case
authoredStages.body: So c² = 25 and c = 5 for this 3-4-5 triangle. This verifies one case; it does not by itself prove the theorem for every right triangle.

widget.successFeedback: Correct for this example: c² = 9 + 16 = 25. The general rearrangement proves the relationship for any right triangle.

steps.body: The rearrangement diagram is the general proof. Both outer squares have side length a + b, and each contains the same four congruent right triangles with legs a and b. In the first arrangement, the area left over is the square c². In the second, the area left over is the two squares a² and b². Subtracting the same four triangles from equal outer squares leaves equal areas, so a² + b² = c² for every right triangle.
Run the identity in reverse: find a missing leg.
explanationVariants: Square both known sides and subtract: 10² − 6² = 100 − 36 = 64, so the missing leg is √64 = 8.
Reverse the identity: hypotenuse-square minus known-leg-square gives the missing leg-square, 64, so the leg is 8.

numericErrors.feedback: That subtracted the LENGTHS (10 − 6) — the identity subtracts the AREAS: 10² − 6² = 64, then √64 = 8.
That's the missing leg's squared AREA (10² − 6² = 64) — take the square root: √64 = 8.

steps.body: The Pythagorean theorem a² + b² = c² is proved by the areas of squares on the sides.
takeaways: The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle — the longest side.
The squares on the two legs add up to the square on the hypotenuse.
That area relationship IS a² + b² = c².
